analysis:
Both supplied units are BASE-side excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 2407-3218). The changed ranges in file_changes are in different regions: head 453-473 (cluster onboarding stop-handling prose), 3239-3242 and 3255-3286. Neither lies in these base excerpts. The patch excerpt is truncated. It describes a documentation-only change: a cluster stop is counted in a setup record (`ClusterSetupRecord.stopsAsked`), and the status reply carries the count (`ClusterControlReply.stopsAsked`). Both Macs compare the count before starting.

The excerpts I reviewed cover Gemma NAX, prefill geometry, deadlines, MTP, sampling defaults and the loop guard. They are unchanged context. They show no new code, wire fields, defaults or trust-boundary changes in this PR. They were not examined for regressions beyond confirming that they are documentation.

The prefix-cache threat T-041 was supplied as a relevant definition, but the visible excerpts do not alter the SSD cache TTL, the HMAC lookup tags or the salt scoping. Documented environment overrides such as DARKBLOOM_CBV2_* are described as disqualifying serving profiles. Nothing in them widens the at-rest surface.

The cluster-stop behavior is only partially visible. The possible security points concern authorization of the `cluster stop` command between peer Macs, and the nil-count handling from older builds, which an older Mac ignores. A peer Mac could in principle report a spoofed `stopsAsked` count to abort onboarding (availability only). The excerpt does not show the real implementation or authentication, and this is a docs-only PR, so no finding is raised. Remaining questions: whether the stop-count comparison runs over the authenticated cluster control channel (TB-014 and cluster trust are not in the supplied evidence), and what the later head ranges (3239-3286) say. Neither could be verified here.
